raw_response:
I will think about this the way I always do — looking at what I did last year and what my neighbors do.

My land is 9 mu. The main thing is the wheat-maize, like everyone here. I will plant wheat and maize on 6 mu together — one after the other in the same field like always. Then 2 mu I will put cotton because my husband's sister's family gets good price from the buyer, and 1 mu mungbean in the corner where the soil is not so good and we eat some at home, sell the rest.

For wheat, I put 2 bags of compound fertilizer (the 15-15-15 kind) before planting — one bag is 50 jin... no wait, 50 kg. Two bags per mu. Then when the wheat wakes up in spring I put urea, about half a bag per mu. My neighbor Old Wang says less is enough but I have seen yellow wheat before and it scared me. Better to put a little extra. Fertilizer costs money but a bad harvest is worse.

For maize after wheat, same thing — one bag compound at planting, then urea when it is knee-high, about half a bag. The maize dealer gives us the hybrid seed, everyone buys from him, it grows strong.

Cotton needs more work. More fertilizer, more spraying — bollworm and aphid come every year. I spray maybe 7 times, my back hurts but if I don't spray I get nothing.

Mungbean I don't put much. It makes its own food somehow, my mother-in-law told me long ago. Just a little fertilizer and one or two sprays.

Well water I have, so I irrigate wheat 4 times — planting, winter water, spring green-up, and when grain fills. Maize 2 times if no rain. Cotton 2-3 times. Mungbean only if very dry.

I use the rotary tiller — the man with the tractor comes through the village, we pay him per mu.
